metrics_computed_not_published: blended_price_per_1m_usd_3to1 is NOT a field the site publishes today (see metrics_lost_since_20260906). It is computed in this scrape as (3 * price1mInputTokens + price1mOutputTokens) / 4, matching the formula implied by the 20260906 scrape's own price1mInputTokens/cost_usd pairs (verified: GLM-4.5V (Non-reasoning) has price1mInputTokens 0.6 and a published cost_usd of 0.9 on 20260906, which is exactly (3*0.6+1.8)/4 with an implied output price of 1.8). The computation is done by the extraction script from the two raw per-token prices already present on every record, not typed by hand. source_field on these rows reads 'computed:price1mInputTokens,price1mOutputTokens' so it is never confused with a site-published field.

notes: Same method as prior scrapes: the data lives in the Next.js App Router RSC flight payload embedded in the leaderboard document, not in a separate XHR/fetch endpoint. window.__next_f is emptied after hydration, so the 56 <script> tags containing `self.__next_f.push(...)` were read out of the DOM and evaluated with a stubbed push() to capture the (id, stringChunk) pairs.

The flight text contains TWO top-level "models":[ arrays, same as before. The slim model-picker list is the first occurrence; the full leaderboard payload (651 entries, confirmed by the presence of intelligenceIndex and gpqa on the first element and length > 100) is the second/last occurrence. Extraction used balanced-bracket, string-aware text slicing and JSON.parse in-browser, and the resulting array was written straight to raw.json via evaluate_script's filePath option - the model never saw or transcribed any row.

raw.json is the verbatim `models` array from that payload: 651 entries, 871,556 bytes, 49 keys observed across the roster (down from 96 on 20260906 - see the site_change_note and the *_lost_since_20260906 lists above for what specifically disappeared and how that was verified).

normalized.json was built afterwards by a local Python script reading raw.json (already machine-written, verbatim) and mechanically emitting one row per (model, benchmark-or-metric); no value was retyped by a human or the agent at any point in the pipeline.

The missing-value sentinel in today's payload is plain JSON null (no literal "$undefined" observed in the captured text). Both forms are treated as absent by the extraction/normalization code regardless.

NEW benchmark row this scrape: Terminal-Bench 4.0 (terminalBench40) - was present as terminalbenchV40 on 20260906 but null on all 643 models; today it carries real scores on 160 of 651 models. This is exactly the kind of newly-populated field the task asked to capture rather than trim away.

Model roster: 651 today vs 643 on 20260906. 9 models are new (e.g. Agnes 3.0 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Reasoning, Max Effort), K2 Horizon 0.9B/3.7B/7B, K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B, Ling-3.0-flash-VL, MiniCPM5-2B, Qwen3.8 Max (0902)). 1 model dropped from the roster: GPT-6 Astra (Non-reasoning) (the other GPT-6 Astra effort variants - low/medium/high/xhigh/max - are all still present).

gdpvalBreakdown, omniscienceBreakdown and any other nested per-category objects remain UNFLATTENED and unexploited in raw.json - same policy as prior scrapes. Browser session note for this run: this MCP session had roughly ten agents scraping different sites concurrently and the shared 'selected page' pointer was stolen on nearly every call - well over 30 consecutive select_page + evaluate_script attempts landed on another agent's page before one hit this page's URL. One of those misses was worse than a simple miss: another agent's navigate_page call actually navigated this page's tab (page id 2, correct isolatedContext name) to benchlm.ai mid-run; this was caught by the href guard, recovered with a second navigate_page back to the target URL, and the page was re-hydrated before extraction resumed. Pure session contention, not a site-side problem.
